# Full ordinary proof candidate: published Remark 3.3(4)

Status: ordinary proof proposed for independent review, NOT accepted, no formal
certificate, no novelty or substantive-eligibility PASS. Root owns these gates.

Let S=C[x1,x2,x3,x4] and pd=sum_i xi^d. For every integer b>2,

    S/(p2,pb) is a domain which is not normal
    iff b=6k+5 or b=12k+8 for an integer k>=1.

This is the literal full classification in Conca–Singh–Soundararajan,
*Ideals generated by power sums*, RRMPA70(2025)49–71,
DOI10.59277/RRMPA.2025.49.71, Remark3.3(4), published p59.
No claim is made for Remark3.3(7), the general CKW conjecture, or extra credit
for any helper/family/normality result.

## 1. Source dependencies and complete reduction

The published Theorem2.3(4) says (p2,pb) is radical; its proof on pp53–54
uses the complete intersection and the Jacobian (R0) condition. Theorem3.1,
with its full Jacobian/root-of-unity proof on pp56–59, says its quotient is
a normal domain precisely when

    b is not 2 modulo4 AND b is not 2 modulo3.

Indeed nu2(2)=1; nu3(2)=0, so the failed second condition is exactly
b=2 modulo3. These are source theorems, not new deductions to count.

When b=2 modulo4, (p2,pb) lies strictly in
(x1-i*x2,x3-i*x4), a prime ideal of the same height2. Strictness follows
from degree1: (p2,pb) contains no nonzero linear form. Thus (p2,pb)
cannot itself be prime. For b=5, Newton identities give p5 in (p1,p2):
modulo that ideal e1=e2=0 and p5=e1*p4-e2*p3+e3*p2-e4*p1=0.
The strict containment in the height2 prime (p1,p2) proves nonprimality;
p2 modulo p1 is a rank3 quadratic form, hence irreducible.

For b=8 put y_i=x_i^2 and
E=y2*y3+y2*y4+y3*y4-y1^2, Z=x1*x2*x3*x4.
Modulo p2, Newton identities for the y's give p8=2(E^2-2Z^2).
Both E-sqrt(2)Z and E+sqrt(2)Z are nonzero modulo (p2,p8):
they have degree4, so vanishing there would mean divisibility by p2;
at (1,i,0,0), p2=0 but each equals -1. Their product is zero in the
quotient, proving nonprimality. These b5/b8 exclusions also appear explicitly
in source Remark3.3(5–6).

The only nonnormal cases left to prove domains are therefore

    b=5 mod6, b>=11;  or  b=8 mod12, b>=20.                 (A)

## 2. Quadric intersection criterion (classical bridge made explicit)

Q=V(p2) in P3 is a smooth quadric over C. A linear change takes it to
X0*X3-X1*X2=0. The Segre parametrization identifies it with P1 x P1.
The two fibers have self-intersection0 and mutual intersection1, as seen by
moving one fiber to a disjoint fiber of the same projection and by intersecting
fibers of opposite projections. Every curve has divisor class (c,d), c,d>=0:
the divisor class group is generated by the two fibers, for example by
trivializing on A1 x A1 and recording poles along the two boundary fibers.
Consequently the intersection of (c,d) and (e,f) is cf+de. A hyperplane
section has class(1,1), hence C_b=V_Q(pb) has class(b,b).
These are ordinary divisor intersection numbers, equivalently the sum of local
intersection lengths when the effective divisors have no common component.

If C_b is reduced and reducible, split its irreducible components into
nonempty disjoint collections D and E. Write [D]=(c,d), [E]=(b-c,b-d).
Their intersection number is

    I=b(c+d)-2cd.                                        (B)

If C_b has only N ordinary nodes as singularities, each intersection of D
and E is one of those nodes, contributes exactly1 (the two branches are
transverse), and no node contributes more than1. Therefore I<=N.

For 0<=c,d<=b with 0<c+d<2b, (B) is at least b. To verify this without
a minimization assumption, put t=c+d; cd<=t^2/4 gives
I>=bt-t^2/2. This concave quadratic on [1,2b-1] has endpoint value b-1/2;
I is integral, so I>=b.
If C_b has no ruling line component then t>=2 and 2b-t>=2:
a nonzero effective class with total degree1 is precisely one ruling line.
The same calculation on [2,2b-2] gives I>=2b-2.
Thus a reduced nodal (b,b) curve is irreducible if N<b, or if it has
no ruling lines and N<2b-2. This is the exact classical mechanism used below;
no general claim that singular curves are irreducible is being invoked.

## 3. Exact singularities: eight or thirty-two, all ordinary nodes

Fix either family (A), and let h=b-2. At a singular projective point of C_b,
the gradients of p2 and pb are dependent. Thus all its nonzero coordinates
have the same h-th power. Scale so one nonzero coordinate is1; all nonzero
coordinates are then h-th roots of unity. Conversely any such point on Q
lies on pb=0 and is singular, since xi^b=xi^2 on its support.

There cannot be one nonzero coordinate. With two nonzero coordinates,
their ratio is +/-i from p2=0. This is impossible because h is odd or
h=2 modulo4, so (+/-i)^h is never1.

There cannot be four nonzero coordinates either. Their squares are four
complex numbers of modulus1 with sum0. Such four numbers can be partitioned
into opposite pairs. Here is a proof covering multiplicities: for a pair z1,z2,
write their sum as w. If w=0 the claim is immediate. Otherwise the unordered
unit pair with sum w is unique: its points are the two intersections of the
unit circle with Re(z*conj(w))=|w|^2/2. Hence {-z3,-z4}={z1,z2}.
An opposite pair of squares would again give coordinate ratio +/-i,
impossible as above.

Exactly three coordinates are nonzero. Normalize the first of these to1.
The other squares are necessarily omega,omega^2 in either order, where
omega is a primitive cube root. Indeed two unit complex numbers summing
to -1 are that pair. The coordinate ratios are therefore sixth roots of
unity with squares omega and omega^2.

For odd b=5 mod6, h is an odd multiple of3. Of the two square roots for
each square, exactly one is an h-th root of1; they are the cube roots
omega,omega^2 themselves. Hence there are two normalized points for each
choice of the zero coordinate: N=4*2=8.
For even b=8 mod12, h=6 mod12. All four sign choices are h-th roots of1.
There are two orders and four signs for each zero coordinate: N=4*2*4=32.
This classification is exhaustive, for arbitrary b in the respective families.

To check node type, work at any normalized singular point x. On its support
xi^h=1. The function F=pb-(b/2)*p2 has gradient0 at x, and its Hessian
is diagonal, with value b(b-2) on each of the three nonzero coordinates
and -b on the zero coordinate. The tangent hyperplane to Q is x dot v=0.
The form sum v_i^2 on the three supported coordinates has radical exactly
C*x upon restriction to x-perp: its ambient form is nondegenerate and x
is isotropic. Quotienting by the radial line thus leaves a nondegenerate
one-dimensional quadratic form. The zero coordinate is an independent
tangent direction with coefficient -b. Both b and b-2 are nonzero over C.
The resulting two-dimensional quadratic form on the projective tangent space
of Q is nondegenerate. The restriction pb|Q consequently has a nondegenerate
quadratic term: an ordinary node, with two transverse branches. For example
at x=(1,omega,omega^2,0), representatives (-omega,1,0,0) and (0,0,0,1)
give Hessian determinant b^2*(b-2)*omega, visibly nonzero.

The source radical theorem already gives reducedness. Alternatively the
exhaustive isolated-singularity analysis forbids a multiple curve component;
source radicality also excludes any affine embedded-origin concern.

## 4. Absence of ruling lines

For even family (A) we also need no line component. Suppose a projective
line lies on Q and pb=0. Restrict each coordinate to a binary linear form
l_i on that line. Group the nonzero forms by proportionality direction.
The b-th powers of at most four pairwise nonproportional binary linear forms
are linearly independent for b>=3. In fact choose binary coordinates so all
directions are u+t_j*v with distinct finite t_j; the coefficients of
u^b,u^(b-1)v,... through the number of directions form a Vandermonde matrix
times nonzero binomial factors.

Since sum l_i^b=0, no proportionality group has size1. The line embedding
has rank2, so there are at least two groups. There are only four coordinates,
hence exactly two groups of two, and no zero coordinate form. Write the
two directions as L,M. Their squares are independent as well, so
sum l_i^2=0 forces the two scalar ratios within the groups to be +/-i.
The cancellation of b-th powers within either group then forces
(+/-i)^b=-1, equivalently b=2 modulo4. The even family (A) has b=0 modulo4,
contradiction. In fact the argument excludes lines for the odd family too.

## 5. Close every source quantifier

For b=6k+5 with k>=1 we have b>=11 and N=8<b. Section2 proves C_b
irreducible. For b=12k+8 with k>=1 we have b>=20, N=32<2b-2, and Section4
excludes ruling lines. Section2 again proves C_b irreducible.
The affine cone over an irreducible projective curve is irreducible, and
(p2,pb) is homogeneous and radical by the source theorem. Its zero set is
exactly this cone, so its ideal is prime by the Nullstellensatz. Thus its
quotient is a domain for all b in (A). Theorem3.1 says each is nonnormal.
Section1 treated all remaining b>2: they are normal domains or are explicitly
not domains. This proves the displayed iff for every source parameter.

## Review objections and limits

No universal mathematical gap is intentionally left. The most important
adversarial checks are the eight-versus-thirty-two count (odd h excludes
the extra signs), ordinary-node multiplicities, the no-lines argument,
and the radical-to-affine-prime transfer. All are spelled out above.
The strong eligibility objection is classical adaptation: source Jacobian
analysis plus elementary quadric intersection theory now gives the result.
Section2 is the complete bridge, not an assertion that shortness implies
exclusion. Root must decide whether node enumeration/type and global
component exclusion amount to substantive new work under this campaign's
standard. No eligibility PASS, priority guarantee, or acceptance is asserted.
